title: Binary Search
statement: Given a sorted list of distinct integers and a target, return the target's index, or -1 if it is not in the list. Aim for O(log n).
brute_force_solution:
def search(nums, target):
    return nums.index(target) if target in nums else -1

hints.1_question: Each comparison should let you throw away half the remaining search space. What do you compare?
hints.2_nudge: Keep lo and hi as the inclusive ends of the range that could still contain the target. Look at the middle element.
hints.3_big_hint: While lo <= hi: mid; if equal return mid; if nums[mid] < target: lo = mid + 1 else hi = mid - 1. Return -1 after the loop.

known_bugs.name: loop condition lo < hi skips the last candidate
known_bugs.followup: With one element, lo and hi are both 0. Does your loop body ever run?

known_bugs.name: hi = mid never shrinks past a miss
known_bugs.followup: You already checked nums[mid] and it was too big. Why keep mid inside the range?

known_bugs.name: comparison direction reversed
known_bugs.followup: If nums[mid] is smaller than the target, which side of mid could the target be on?

followups: How could `(lo + hi) // 2` overflow in languages like Java, and what is the safe form?
Write the same search with the half-open range [lo, hi). What changes?
